content_voiceover: This slide covers CLL prognostic markers and the CLL International Prognostic Index, or CLL-IPI. On the left, prognostic testing methods include interphase FISH cytogenetics, DNA sequencing, and CpG stimulated metaphase karyotype. By FISH, deletion seventeen p and deletion eleven q are unfavorable, trisomy twelve and a normal karyotype are intermediate, and deletion thirteen q as a sole abnormality is favorable, the best prognosis subgroup. By sequencing, wild type TP53 and IGHV mutation greater than two percent are favorable, while TP53 mutation and unmutated IGHV, meaning two percent or less, are unfavorable. A complex karyotype with three or more unrelated clonal abnormalities is also unfavorable. On the right, the CLL-IPI combines five weighted factors, age over sixty, Binet B or C or Rai one through four, serum beta-2 microglobulin over three point five, unmutated IGHV, and TP53 abnormality, either seventeen p deletion or TP53 mutation, which carries the heaviest weight of four points. Total scores stratify patients into low, intermediate, high, and very high risk groups, guiding both prognosis discussion and treatment intensity.
keypoints: Deletion seventeen p and TP53 mutation are the worst prognostic markers
Deletion thirteen q alone carries the best prognosis
CLL-IPI score combines age, stage, beta-2 microglobulin, IGHV, and TP53
TP53 abnormality weighs four points, the heaviest single factor
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, know that TP53 mutation or deletion seventeen p is the single worst prognostic factor, weighted four points in the CLL-IPI, while deletion thirteen q alone is the most favorable. The CLL-IPI score combines age, clinical stage, beta-2 microglobulin, IGHV mutation status, and TP53 status to sort patients into four risk tiers.
